description: We are Zephyr, a team passionate about science, technology, and innovation. We combine Artificial Intelligence, programming, and data analysis to explore climate trends and transform Earth observation data into accessible insights, helping society better understand environmental changes and make sustainable decisions.
summary:
Zephyr is an interactive platform for exploring the infrared sky and investigating changes across astronomical observations. We developed a laboratory that combines SPHEREx imagery, spanning 102 spectral channels across six detectors, with complementary information from Gaia DR3, AllWISE, and NEOWISE.
Users can search sky coordinates, look up object identifiers through the Minor Planet Center, select observation periods and spectral ranges, and compare exposures using animations, image stacks, and difference views. The platform also provides false-color mosaics for visual exploration, flux plots, and aperture photometry measurements.
Processing preserves calibration, uncertainties, and available coverage while flagging invalid pixels and potential stellar contamination. Through an accessible interface and traceable results, Zephyr brings open scientific data closer to students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts, supporting investigations of motion and apparent variability without presenting candidates as confirmed discoveries.
details:
Zephyr is an astronomical exploration platform that transforms public infrared sky data into an interactive visual experience. Its goal is to make observations from different times easier to compare, helping users investigate object motion and apparent brightness changes while providing the information needed to interpret the results.

How it works

The laboratory uses SPHEREx FITS images and lets users select coordinates, observation periods, detectors, and wavelength ranges across its 102 spectral channels. Integration with the Minor Planet Center supports object identification and helps prepare observation searches in the IRSA archive.

The platform also cross-matches positions with Gaia DR3, AllWISE, and NEOWISE, considering coordinates and temporal compatibility. Each source retains its role: SPHEREx provides the infrared images and measurements being analyzed; Gaia supplies stellar context; WISE and NEOWISE contribute complementary records and imagery from other observations.

Users can explore results through time animations, image stacks, difference images, flux plots, and aperture photometry. False-color mosaics combine infrared bands to make structures easier to visualize. These colors serve aesthetic and interpretive purposes, while scientific measurements remain tied to calibrated data.

Benefits and intended impact

Zephyr lowers the technical barrier to working with astronomical files. Within one interface, users can search observations, compare images, inspect data quality, and export traceable results.

We aim to support science education, independent exploration, and the preparation of investigations into moving objects and potential variability. The platform encourages critical use of open data: a visual change can guide further analysis, but does not establish a confirmed discovery on its own.

Tools and technologies

We developed the processing pipeline in Python, using tools such as Astropy and NumPy for FITS handling, celestial coordinates, and numerical operations. The interface uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Canvas rendering for images and plots. We also used Node.js, automated tests, and Git/GitHub for validation, version control, and collaboration.

The solution runs in a browser with a local processing server and requires no dedicated astronomical hardware.

Creativity and team considerations

The creative aspect lies in bringing temporal exploration, spectral selection, catalogue context, and color compositions together in an accessible laboratory. Users can move between an intuitive view of the sky and the technical details supporting each image.

The team considered interface clarity, desktop and mobile navigation, performance, and scientific responsibility. We preserve coverage gaps, flag invalid pixels and potential stellar contamination, and provide uncertainties and provenance. We also account for the fact that observations from different epochs and filters should not be treated as a simultaneous spectrum or a fixed-band light curve.
